question: Does every product of two one-bit decorations of the pinwheel (a pair of bits per tile, each passed to the children by its own one-bit decoration) admit one of the crystals in hand: a periodic two-bit labelling of the crystal's cut obeying the product's labelled law? The products that admit none are the candidates for two bits forcing the pinwheel.

public_inputs.products: All 1,048,576 ordered pairs of one-bit decorations, taken up to exchanging the factors and relabelling either factor (s~(b) = 1 - s(1 - b)); a product's law is ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001A's decor_lib labelled closure with the four labels 2a + b.
public_inputs.crystals: The 11 domino-torus planes legal within two cuts (ONE-BIT-20261108-001B's kept planes, the rhombus lattice and brick rows among them) at their first legal cut j and at j + 1, and the 26 mixed-orientation crystals of CRYSTAL-UP-20261108-001A (CRYSTAL-UP-20261108-001B's crystal.json) at one and two cuts; tori of index 1 or 2 over each plane's lattice. A test is a plane, a number of cuts and a torus.
public_inputs.one-bit table: For each of the 1,024 one-bit decorations, the tests its law admits (decor_lib.periodic), levels tried in order on each plane and torus, admission at one level giving the next (ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001A, Lemma 2).
public_inputs.product test: For each product class, the tests both factors admit, cheapest first (tiles per period times 5^cuts times torus index); each a SAT model of a periodic labelling with two variables per tile obeying the product's law. The first admitted test is the product's escape; a product with none is a survivor. No other test can admit a product: its labels project to an escape of each factor.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the crystals, levels, tori or the product test after seeing results
primary_observable: The number of product classes that escape no listed crystal (the survivors), and which they are.
secondary_observables: The one-bit table (which tests each one-bit decoration admits); the escapes by crystal family; the number of tests tried per product.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Positive: every one-bit decoration admits some listed test (each of the 1,024 is known to escape a crystal in the list: the domino planes for 1,022, the mixed crystals for the last two); every product with the constant decoration 00000 / 11111 escapes. A run whose controls fail is not read.
first_executable_signal: The one-bit table and its control.
decision_or_followup_rule: The epic's frozen stop rule: if every product class escapes a listed crystal, no product of one-bit decorations forces the pinwheel (each escape is a crystal at every radius, by the radius lemma) and the line pauses; if some escape none, one bounded forcing test runs on them (ticket B) and the line pauses after it.
stop_rule: Stop at the declared products, crystals, levels and tori.
nonclaims: Exploratory: a survivor escapes none of the listed crystals, which does not show that it forces the pinwheel.
Two-bit decorations that are not products are not tested.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing: a product's four-label law takes milliseconds once the skeleton is built (1,240 to 2,132 labelled collars on three samples); 64 one-bit laws with tests at one and two cuts on the 8-tile mixed crystal took 0.4 seconds. A probe of this run on its first 3,000 product classes (without the level shortcut in the one-bit table) was started before freezing; its timing is reported in this run's interpretation.
